parts: You see the flash. Now count. One second. Five. Ten.
Only then does the thunder arrive.
Environment Canada says light travels three hundred thousand kilometers per second. Sound, about three tenths.
Our arithmetic: light is about a million times faster.
The National Weather Service says thunder takes about five seconds to travel a mile.
Our comparison: the delay is a tape measure.
Count the seconds, then divide by five for miles, or by three for kilometers.
Our arithmetic: ten seconds is about two miles.
Sound moves faster in hot air and slower in cold air.
